💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that maine's Gambling Control Unit is heading toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos after a single public hearing.
  • Maine’s regulator is moving toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos.
  • Maine will become the eighth state with legal online casinos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that maine's Gambling Control Unit is heading toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos after a single public hearing. A former lawmaker warns that the state's behavioral health system is too thin for a possible rise in gambling addiction, while a federal lawsuit still targets the tribes' exclusivity.

Maine’s regulator is moving toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos. Only one public hearing has been held so far. WGME’s I-Team reported on Nov. 16 that the Gambling Control Unit began iGaming rulemaking in June. Residents in the report raised a separate concern. They worry the state lacks the mental health and problem-gambling resources to cope.

Maine will become the eighth state with legal online casinos. Its four Wabanaki tribes hold exclusive licenses under LD 1164, the Wabanaki internet gaming act. The Legislature lists the measure as enacted as Public Law 538.

Sources indicate that the money set aside for addiction services is small next to the state’s cut. The legislative fiscal note sends 2% of adjusted gross iGaming receipts to the Gambling Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund. The state’s own 18% share is projected at $1.8 million in fiscal 2025-26 and $3.6 million in fiscal 2026-27.

Critics doubt the system can absorb the demand. Patty Locuratolo Hymanson, a neurologist and former state lawmaker, told WGME that Maine lacks the behavioral health resources to handle a possible rise in gambling addiction from online casinos.

Lawmakers reshaped the revenue split before passage. A committee amendment raised the state’s share from 16% to 18%. The same amendment cut the opioid treatment fund’s allocation from 3% to 1.5%. The fiscal note also carries ongoing General Fund appropriations of $645,354 for six Gambling Control Unit positions. Those include two criminal intelligence analysts and two auditors.

It has been revealed that the regulator itself was skeptical at first. Before the bill became law, Executive Director Milt Champion opposed it in written testimony. He argued iGaming wasn’t warranted while sports wagering was only in its second year.

It has been revealed that rulemaking is still underway. The unit issued its third version of the draft rules on Sept. 30, 2026, and took comments until Oct. 30. Champion has warned that major revisions would force a fourth publication. The third draft keeps the tax rate on adjusted gross receipts unchanged. It also retains the license fee and bond requirements. The regulator is hiring six staff members dedicated to iGaming.

The launch also faces a court fight over tribal exclusivity. Churchill Downs and Oxford Casino Hotel brought their suit against the Gambling Control Unit and Champion in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maine. They are asking the court to declare the law unconstitutional. The challenge goes to the heart of the market’s design, which reserves online casino licenses for the tribes.

The next deadlines are procedural. Under Maine’s rulemaking law, the unit has up to 120 days after comments close to adopt the rules. The Attorney General’s office has up to 150 days from that same date to approve them as legal. The unit’s rulemaking page also lists a public hearing notice marked Nov. 30, 2026, which could change that timetable.

Latest Update: Can you fix a scratched CD? Here are your options

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can try toothpaste or wax, but do so at your own risk.
  • Recent findings suggest that just like vinyl records before them, CDs are back.
  • The first step to fixing a CD that's skipping or not playing is to see if it just needs to be cleaned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can try toothpaste or wax, but do so at your own risk.

Recent findings suggest that just like vinyl records before them, CDs are back. As strange as it may seem if you grew up with them, CDs have become a nostalgic icon of the joys of physical media — but they're also a reminder of why we all went digital in the first place. The biggest drawback of CDs was always just how easy it can be to ruin one with a careless scratch, and that hasn't changed. If you're embracing CDs for the first time or taking them for a spin again because of the CD revival, a scratch may seem like the end for your favorite album, but there are a few time-tested ways to get your discs back in playing shape.

The first step to fixing a CD that's skipping or not playing is to see if it just needs to be cleaned. Oils from your hands and debris like dust can cause playback issues without actually damaging the disc and they're easy enough to wipe away. To start, grab a lint-free cloth like microfiber and use it to wipe the CD from the center to the outer edge. Don't wipe across the CD, as this can cause more damage. For really dirty discs, you can use a little 70 percent isopropyl alcohol or distilled water applied to the cloth, though this typically isn't necessary. If you use any kind of liquid, make sure it's completely dried before you try to play or store your discs.

For deeper scratches, there are a few time-tested DIY methods you'll find recommended often, but none of them are foolproof. Keep in mind that if you're taking disc repair into your own hands, there's no guarantee that you'll actually make things better, and there's some chance you'll make the problem worse. That being remarked, it's entirely possible to buff out scratches and make CDs playable again, but whether it works depends on just how bad the damage is in the first place. For DIY disc repair, the goal is to use some form of abrasive to sand down the layer of the CD with a scratch, letting the player's laser reach the data stored deeper in the disc.

Toothpaste is one of the most common cleaners to use, since it's cheap, accessible and not too damaging. Make sure you have plain white toothpaste without any gels, beads or whitening agents, and squirt a bit on the disc. Spread it evenly, then use a lint-free cloth to wipe from the inside of the disc outward a few times, all around the disc. Then rinse it off with water and let it dry. You can perform the same process with a stronger abrasive like 3M rubbing compound if you prefer.

In a recent development, if your disc still doesn't work, you can apply a thin layer of wax (like shoe polish or Chapstick) to seal the scratches. Just apply the wax from the inside of the disc to the outside and wipe it away using the same motion after a few minutes. Remember to let any product you apply dry completely before using your disc.

Sources indicate that for scratches you can't get out yourself, disc repair services are also an option, though they're rare these days and you may not have one near you. These services use professional-grade machines that essentially buff discs the same way that home methods do, but they can be more reliable. If you're really serious about preserving your discs, you can also buy one of these high-end machines yourself, but since they can run into the thousands of dollars, it's not an option for most people. In most cases, seeking professional repair or buying a disc repair machine only makes sense if you're trying to preserve rare CDs with material you can't find elsewhere.

If you want to preserve the data on your CD and you're not precious about the disc itself, it's a good idea to invest in a CD burner. This lets you copy the data on the disc, keeping it safe even if the physical CD is damaged. Making copies is a good idea, since your CD collection won't last forever. In some cases, a burner may be able to record the data from a disc even when scratches are causing it to skip in your CD player, letting you make another copy later. Like with any repair method, the success of a CD burner depends on how damaged the disc is, but it's a non-destructive way of preserving your CD's contents when it works.

#3229. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are Everywhere

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2188 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are Everywhere

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2188 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
  • But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto.
  • Something must be behind all of this, you might think — a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

Microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some concerns. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

Something must be behind all of this, you might think — a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these concerns, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

Adam Meyers, senior vice president of counteradversary operations at cybersecurity manufacturer CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

“This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

One substantial reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

If it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

Artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a big or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

At the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should upgrade. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

According to recent reports, another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

When I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he remarked, “it’s bad.”.

Recent findings suggest that as owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He says he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. Latest AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

“You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand said.

Things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning.

In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers notes CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

“Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers said.

Despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

“The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” said Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

In a recent development, the good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

It still might not be enough, and Massive Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

And defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated at the Newly introduced York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

That’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

“There’s effectively this major backlog of security issues in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” said Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity tech giant focused on connected devices.

It has been revealed that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

“Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse said.

Wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of issues is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with important, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to update so frequently these days.

“It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” said Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

And patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s complications on Tuesday.

Sources indicate that things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents latest problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing problem.

Recent findings suggest that in the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

Massive Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

“I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” said Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy states.

That means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into fresh software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

In a recent development, the main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

“I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he remarked. “It will hurt a bit.”.

Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more vital than ever.

“You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers remarked. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

In a recent development, but consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a organization isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

In a recent development, we don’t have to put up with it, Barlet says. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he said.

Android's sideloading freedom is about to get a lot more complicated worldwide

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Androidcentral

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for quite a long time, Android has had one significant advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission.
  • Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the manufacturer.
  • In a recent development, confirmed in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for quite a long time, Android has had one significant advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission. That freedom is about to come with considerably more friction.

Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the manufacturer.

In a recent development, confirmed in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed. The new rules will also apply to third-party app marketplaces and independently distributed APKs.

Google is working with seven distributors, including Google Play, Samsung’s Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo, to bring the requirements to more users.

Google says the changes are intended to make it more difficult for scammers and malicious developers to continue distributing harmful apps. The firm says millions of applications have already been registered, representing more than 99% of Android app installs worldwide. The launch began on September 30, 2026, in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.

According to recent reports, but developers won’t be the only ones feeling the shift. To install unverified apps, you’ll have to take extra steps. You’ll have to authenticate your device and make sure you’re not being forced to change your security settings. After this, restart your phone and wait 24 hours before you can enable unrestricted sideloading.

Google does offer an advanced install option for power users who want to skip verification, but it’s not quite the one-tap experience Android enthusiasts have grown accustomed to.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

In a recent development, there are also concessions for smaller developers. Free limited-distribution accounts allow students and hobbyists to share apps with up to 50 authorized devices without having to verify their identity with a government ID or pay registration fees. Google has also added APIs to make it easier for developers with multiple apps to register.

But the bigger question is what this change means for Android’s reputation as an open platform. Google says consumers can still choose where they download their apps from, but the freedom is made a lot less convenient by adding identity checks, restrictions on installation, and a mandatory waiting period.

After the global rollout, protections are expected to be available to all countries and installation sources over the span of a few months. Google documentation states that full enforcement is expected on March 1, 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • MCP is short for Model Context Protocol, an open standard that lets AI assistants plug into outside tools.
  • Canva becomes the design layer inside Claude with upcoming Anthropic partnership.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Canva MCP — any agent or AI assistant.

Canva is opening its design tools to AI agents and to developers building other products. The tech giant has made its MCP server generally available with no waitlist, and added newly introduced APIs so Canva can run inside other software rather than only in its own apps.

MCP is short for Model Context Protocol, an open standard that lets AI assistants plug into outside tools. Canva’s server, built on it, already powers millions of design tasks inside assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.

Canva becomes the design layer inside Claude with upcoming Anthropic partnership.

Moreover, Canva claims nearly 500,000 people have signed up through MCP since October, and that usage grew 93% in a month.

The organization has also rebuilt the server around how agents behave, merging overlapping tools so that even agents running on smaller models pick the right one. Agents can now generate editable designs, images, and video, remove backgrounds, turn flat images into layered files, and resize and export the finished work.

In a recent development, for someone sitting in a chat, it works like this: ask for an Instagram post, and back comes a real Canva design in the brand’s own colours and fonts. The result opens in an editing panel beside the conversation, so a wonky headline gets fixed by hand rather than by another round of prompting.

Video gets the same treatment, as an agent can turn out a short product clip, voiceover included, and hand it back on an editable timeline rather than as a finished file nobody can change.

Sources indicate that developers who want more control can reach the same features through upcoming REST APIs instead, and a command-line tool covers bulk jobs. That tool’s main users are already agents, which Canva indicates typed 72% of its commands in October.

For bigger companies, latest service accounts and API billing let automated workflows run without an employee being signed in. People using a product built on Canva won’t each need a Canva account of their own, while the developer manages usage and costs.

According to recent reports, canva is also opening up Craft, its in-house image generation model, through the API and MCP. The models, built by Canva Research for design and editing work, were until now only available inside Canva’s own products.

Sources indicate that canva states four in ten people arriving through MCP are newly introduced to the product or returning after a long absence. Those who come in through an AI assistant are 2.5 times more likely to use its AI tools. The yearly revenue it expects from MCP has more than tripled since September.

The pitch to other companies is a simple one: any product whose people need to make something can now carry Canva inside it, without building design tools of its own.

All of it serves an ambition Canva calls “the design layer of the internet”: being the technology other products build on whenever their customers need to create something.

#3226. Tech Report: What you can do with your old, discontinued Mac Pro

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (910 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: What you can do with your old, discontinued Mac Pro

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this year, Apple discontinued its Mac Pro desktop workstation, marking an end to one of the organization's longest-running product lines.
  • Whether you decide to sell your Mac Pro to finance an upgrade to a new Mac Studio, repurpose the existing hardware with a new operating system or simply continue to use the workstation for years to come, you have plenty of options.
  • Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026 in order to prioritize the upcoming Mac Studio line of workstations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mac Pros are becoming obsolete. Do they still have use?

Earlier this year, Apple discontinued its Mac Pro desktop workstation, marking an end to one of the organization's longest-running product lines. Starting at $5,999 for the entry-level 2019 model and costing tens of thousands of dollars when fully equipped, the Mac Pro was (and still is) a serious investment for most people and companies. Thankfully, even though Apple has stopped making newly introduced Mac Pros, your discontinued workstation is hardly worthless.

Whether you decide to sell your Mac Pro to finance an upgrade to a new Mac Studio, repurpose the existing hardware with a new operating system or simply continue to use the workstation for years to come, you have plenty of options. The secondhand market for Mac Pros remains strong, while the modular nature of the Mac Pro means that running alternative operating systems to keep the device current is easier than it is with newer Mac products. Plus, if it's in working condition, there's nothing stopping you from continuing to use it as intended, even if its hardware is showing its age. Regardless of what you're looking to do, here's everything you need to know about what comes next for your discontinued Mac Pro and how to get the most value out of it.

Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026 in order to prioritize the upcoming Mac Studio line of workstations. With the move to Apple silicon, which uses a highly integrated system-on-a-chip (SoC) design, a modular desktop workstation like the Mac Pro no longer makes sense. Drop-in cards like GPUs aren't compatible with Apple's in-house silicon due to Apple's use of a unified memory architecture for the Apple M-series chips. This architecture shares memory resources across the CPU, GPU and other system components, and there simply isn't a good way to introduce some third-party components commonly used with the 2019 Mac Pro. The 2023 Mac Pro, meanwhile, uses the Apple M2 Ultra SoC and lacks the modularity of the 2019 model, so it's essentially a Mac Studio in a Mac Pro shell.

Apple is also streamlining macOS around its SoC design, something that developers for popular professional software like Adobe Premiere Pro are also doing. Since it would be too cumbersome to develop this kind of sophisticated software for two different kinds of Apple architectures, Apple and its partners are focusing on what's upcoming rather than trying to continue supporting an increasingly obsolete architecture. Without sufficient software support, it makes little sense to continue producing the Mac Pro.

According to recent reports, while Apple isn't producing new Mac Pros, that doesn't mean you have to get rid of yours. Developers are streamlining their apps for Apple M-series Macs, but some app support for Intel-based Macs will likely continue for another couple of years, like security updates and minor fixes. This support will vary between developers, though, and Apple's latest macOS 27 Golden Gate doesn't support the Intel-based Mac Pro.

Recent findings suggest that if you have the 2023 Mac Pro, you don't have anything to worry about right now. It will be supported for years to come, and that support includes macOS 27 Golden Gate. Third-party apps will also support the 2023 Mac Pro for as long as they support the Apple M2 Ultra SoC.

If you're not getting the support you need from macOS on your old Mac Pro, you can install a new OS, either with a virtual machine or through a completely new installation. A guest OS doesn't get rid of macOS, and paid apps like Parallels make installing Ubuntu Linux and Windows 11 relatively painless. There are also free VM options that can help extend your discontinued Mac Pro's life.

Attempting a full install of a new OS might also be an option, but it's a complicated process and comes with some risk of bricking your Mac Pro for good. There are online resources to walk you through the process, but you'll need some technical know-how, so if you aren't comfortable with that, do not attempt it.

It has been revealed that if you're going to get rid of your old Mac Pro, don't just recycle it — plenty of people will be willing to buy it from you. Many professional workflows, like video editing or running a network server, require a lot of memory but don't necessarily need the fastest processors. Professionals and students in those fields might jump at the chance to pick up a working Mac Pro for relatively cheap. Online marketplaces are good places to start, but a handwritten bulletin board notice at your local university can work just as well.

Industry observers note that if you have a 2019 Mac Pro, its internal components might also be worth selling individually. Memory and large-capacity storage drives are especially in-demand right now, so even though stripping your Mac Pro for parts might feel unseemly, if you can't find a buyer for the whole system, this might be the way to go. Some money is better than nothing.

If you initiative on getting rid of your Mac Pro, make sure to do a few things beforehand. Read through this support page on Apple's website and follow the instructions for backing up your files, logging out of accounts and performing a factory reset. The last thing you want is to give someone all your sensitive data after saying goodbye to your old Mac Pro for good.

It has been revealed that nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he stepped down, and less than a week after the company's board said it had no intention of bringing him back. Reactions to Huang's return have been a mix of praise, criticism, and jokes, with several other tech executives rallying around him.

Sources indicate that nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Nov. 12, a day after the board accepted it with immediate effect. He stepped down amid reports that he'd had extramarital affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and a Nvidia employee, with allegations of a third affair with another worker subsequently surfacing. His relationship with Alice Huang (no relation) drew particular scrutiny, as she was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips. She previously led Megaspeed, a company U.S. authorities have been investigating over concerns it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of U.S. restrictions.

While Huang stated that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if asked, the board stated said on Nov. 17 that it did not initiative to bring him back. Yet after reported pressure from President Donald Trump, the chipmaker has put Huang back in the top job after all. In a press release announcing Huang's reinstatement, Nvidia stated that it had based the decision on "input from senior levels of the United States government.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," remarked Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones, who last week said that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen.".

Trump has been characteristically celebratory about Nvidia's decision, making several posts on his social media platform Truth Social on the topic. This included an edited image based on a photo of Trump after a shooter attempted to assassinate him in 2024. Originally posted by X account @grandoldmemes, the picture has been edited to show Huang holding a red bra aloft as a Nvidia banner is displayed in the background.

According to recent reports, calling Huang's reinstatement an "absolutely GREAT decision" (emphasis original), Trump stated that having him installed as Nvidia's CEO is vital to the U.S. economy.

Recent findings suggest that "The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Tech giant, but the American Economy," wrote Trump. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security…. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure.".

Industry observers note that the U.S. president also spoke about Huang's reinstatement in a phone call to CNBC on Monday.

"I think he's gonna start off at an almost higher level," Trump mentioned. "He's apologised for [his] indiscretion, which was unfortunate. Probably that’s what brought it to such a level, because sex sells, fellas. Now [CNBC host Jim] Cramer would not know that because he’s a very, very, very committed person. But sex sells.".

Trump's on-and-off ally Elon Musk also celebrated Huang's return, reposting Nvidia's announcement on X and writing that "the mistake has been corrected." Last week, Musk stated that he was signing a petition to reinstate Nvidia's then-ousted CEO.

According to recent reports, "Everyone I know at Nvidia wanted Jensen back and it shows," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO continued, sharing a post from investor Gavin Baker. In it, Baker shared images of people crowding around Huang and applauding him on his return to Nvidia's offices.

According to recent reports, "Grateful to the President, everyone in the administration, everyone who signed the petition, everyone who supported Jensen publicly, everyone who called the board, everyone on the board who fought for him, everyone," Baker wrote. Various other prominent figures in tech have also voiced support for Huang's return, several of whom have previously faced comparable turmoil at their own companies.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman appeared to express approval for Huang's reinstatement, publishing a post on X that simply read, "Jensen!" Altman went through a similar incident when OpenAI's board fired him in 2023, accusing him of lying, retaliating against critics, and creating a "toxic atmosphere." Despite these allegations, Altman was ultimately reinstated after days of outcry from supporters.

Meanwhile, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao posted to X that he was "glad to see @JensenHuang back," resharing his previous reaction that it was "a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign." Zhao resigned from his role as CEO of Binance and pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program in 2023, serving a four-month prison sentence. However, he remains Binance's majority shareholder and retains significant influence over the global cryptocurrency exchange.

According to recent reports, "Jensen is a great man, flawed like the rest of us, but at the same time the best amongst us," Kalanick posted to X on Monday. "The world and humanity needs him to fight for a shot at liberty, a counterweight to techno-authoritarianism.".

Kalanick resigned from his role as Uber CEO in 2017 after demands from multiple major investors. This came after Kalanick took a leave of absence amid allegations of a misogynistic workplace culture. Though one of the investors sued Kalanick for fraud later that year, the ousted CEO remained on Uber's board until resigning in 2019.

Recent findings suggest that telegram CEO Pavel Durov also celebrated Huang's return, posting "Jensen's back" with a party popper emoji. He then joked about the situation, writing that "Nvidia's board finally accepted that a CEO has to evaluate Chinese models personally. You can't delegate that.".

According to recent reports, durov was ousted from his former role as CEO of Russian social media platform VK in 2014 after the board said it had accepted a resignation he'd submitted and failed to withdraw. Durov claimed the resignation had been an April Fools' joke and suggested that his firing was politically motivated.

Industry observers note that given their own personal experiences, it's no surprise that many former and current tech executives have supported Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO. Other reactions have been a mixed bag — some celebrating the news, some condemning it, and others simply enjoying the jokes and memes.

"Reinstating Huang is a disaster for corporate governance and even the rule of law, but it is objectively very very funny," author and tech reporter David Z. Morris posted to X.

Some have also noted the timing of Huang's temporary ousting, joking that he deliberately orchestrated several days away from work in order to play Grand Theft Auto VI.

In a recent development, it's been a tumultuous few weeks for Nvidia, and it's unclear how the company plans to move forward at this stage. However, whatever happens, the jokes will likely continue for a while.

Recent findings suggest that generative AI continues to draw widespread skepticism from both local communities and everyday internet users. “By integrating Dott benefits straight into the Revolut app, we are making sustainable urban travel even more rewarding and accessible across key European cities.”.

It now runs 200,000 shared vehicles across 400 cities in Europe and the Middle East, and says its 12 million owners have taken more than 500 million rides so far.

Putting its vehicles inside bigger consumer apps has become a habit for Dott. A similar deal in April put free monthly rides inside Wolt’s subscription scheme in eight countries, and Dott vehicles already appear in the FREE NOW and Citymapper apps.

Sources indicate that the draw for Dott is Revolut’s reach: more than 80 million customers, who make over a billion transactions a month between them. The fintech also remains Europe’s most valuable private tech firm.

#3216. Commons reasons your Android phone's icons won't move and how to fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (528 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Commons reasons your Android phone's icons won't move and how to fix it

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (528 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Android phones offer plenty of customization options to help you organize your apps.
  • It has been revealed that many Android phones can auto-arrange icons in your app drawer, usually called automatic sorting.
  • If your icons aren't moving at all, check your home screen and launcher cache settings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s most likely your home screen settings.

Android phones offer plenty of customization options to help you organize your apps. Some settings, unbeknownst to customers, can reorganize your phone's icons or prevent you from moving them at all. A home screen that keeps changing can be frustrating, but the good news is you can fix it without much troubleshooting.

It has been revealed that many Android phones can auto-arrange icons in your app drawer, usually called automatic sorting. This causes your phone to organize icons in alphabetical order, by install date or by other listed criteria. App or OS updates can also change your home screen grid, so don't be alarmed if icons rearrange after a major software revision.

If your icons aren't moving at all, check your home screen and launcher cache settings. A locked home screen is the main culprit on most phones. However, if you're using a Google Pixel or stock Android without a locked home screen setting, clearing your launcher cache is another option. Employing either solution is fairly straightforward.

The most likely cause of locked icons is a locked home screen. Many Android manufacturers enable locked home screens by default, preventing you from moving icons. You can fix this by going into your phone's home screen settings and turning the setting off.

Most Samsung phones let you access this setting by going to Settings and searching for "Home Screen." From there, look for the option "Lock Home Screen Layout." Toggle it off to enable icon movement again. If you are using another type of Android device, you can usually find this setting under the "Home" tab of your device.

Recent findings suggest that once you've unlocked your home screen, you might notice that your icons will sometimes reorganize themselves without your input. This could be due to some auto-sort options in your phone settings. You can find these sorting options in your home screen settings—on Samsung phones, under "Settings," while on some Android phones, under "Home." If your home screen layout is still not to your liking, consider resetting your home screen and restart your phone.

On Android devices without a locked home screen layout, such as Google Pixel phones, you may want to clear your launcher cache instead. Your phone's launcher cache saves all temporary data related to your home screen. If this cache gets bloated, it can make your phone more prone to crashing and cause inconsistent home screen behavior, including frozen icons.

Clearing the launcher cache is similar across Android phones, though the launcher app varies by manufacturer. Head to your phone's settings menu and look through your apps. You're looking for your phone's launcher. Google Pixel uses the Pixel Launcher; Samsung phones use One UI. Select the app and head to its storage settings. You should see an option to clear its cache. After you clear it, you should notice your home screen is more responsive. We also suggest rebooting your phone once you've cleared the cache to ensure it actually gets cleared out. If your phone remains unresponsive, restart your phone in safe mode to see whether a third-party app is causing the problem.

#3211. The biggest downsides to using Apple's Magic Mouse

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (727 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

The biggest downsides to using Apple's Magic Mouse

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (727 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple switched the Magic Mouse to USB-C but left its most questionable design decision untouched, and that isn’t the only thing users dislike.
  • Sources indicate that there are a handful of things that Apple's Magic Mouse does that would make regular mice envious.
  • And it isn't the only reason even committed Mac customers are calling it quits on the official Apple mouse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple switched the Magic Mouse to USB-C but left its most questionable design decision untouched, and that isn’t the only thing users dislike.

Sources indicate that there are a handful of things that Apple's Magic Mouse does that would make regular mice envious. The shimmery Multi-Touch surface lets you scroll sideways on a spreadsheet and move across macOS even without that conventional scroll wheel. But then, it is also brilliantly designed to be unusable when the charging cable is plugged in. That's not a small trade-off, especially for a device whose very purpose is to make computer use a breeze.

And it isn't the only reason even committed Mac customers are calling it quits on the official Apple mouse. The weirdly slender body looks gorgeous but offers barely any palm space, while the aluminum sides aren't universally loved either. For those who've used a traditional mouse for years, the controls on the Magic Mouse can also feel severely limiting.

Even after ditching the Lightning port with the 2024 refresh alongside the much faster M4 iMac, Apple decided to leave most of those pain points untouched. Now, in all honesty, the Magic Mouse has a pretty strong fan base, especially among owners who love its touch gestures and that classic Apple minimalist design. But if you're spending hours using it, the things it cuts out can matter a lot more than the cool tricks it has.

Apple unveiled the rechargeable Magic Mouse 2 back in October 2015 with its Lightning port at the bottom. A seemingly controversial design choice even back then, it somehow survived the switch to USB-C almost a decade later. So, every time your Magic Mouse is out of juice, you need to flip it over and leave it be until there's enough power to start using the mouse again.

The saving grace here is that the mouse's battery is good for around a month or more between charges, so flipping your Magic Mouse on its back isn't a daily ordeal. But that doesn't make it any less weird, especially since Apple allows its Magic Keyboard and Magic Trackpad to be used while they're plugged in. There's also no clarity from Apple on how many years the rechargeable battery in the Magic Mouse is expected to last.

Now, let's talk about that shape which puts this slim mouse at just 0.85 inches tall. There's also barely any palm support, and depending on how you're holding it, those aluminum edges can press uncomfortably against your fingers. If you use a fingertip grip, this might be less of a problem, but if you're more of a "resting your entire hand on a mouse" type of person, adjusting your grip is something you'll have to get used to.

In a recent development, since Apple is asking $79 for the Magic Mouse in white and $99 for the black version, you'd expect the basic functions. While Apple's mouse supports right-clicking with its touch-sensitive surface, there's no middle-click or a programmable thumb button. Using CAD software is where you miss those buttons the most, since holding the middle mouse button is how you usually pan around drawings. Sure, third-party utilities can add some of the missing functionality, but having to install extra software to bring conventional features to a premium mouse is frustrating to say the least.

Sources indicate that you've got to give some credit to the Multi-Touch surface, especially for making scrolling without the usual wheel still feel natural. But do expect accidental swipes like you would on a phone screen since there are no physical controls. Some owners have even faced challenges like stuttering and inconsistent tracking. Those could very well be isolated incidents though, and in one case, the lag started right after a macOS update.

Recent findings suggest that the good part is that Apple doesn't force the Magic Mouse down your throat just because you own a Mac. You can use one of the best wireless mice from other brands on macOS, although you would be missing out on gestures that make the Magic Mouse so special. Logitech's Signature M650, for instance, packs a typical scroll wheel and comes equipped with physical side buttons. Costing about half as much as the Magic Mouse at $39.99, the M650 comes with a contoured grip in place of the Magic Mouse's glossy finish.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.
  • Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX.
  • In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down.

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones remarked in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones said. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this manufacturer accountable.”.

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”.

Grok Imagine introduced on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

“It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield stated in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

In a recent development, in a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX remarked that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”.

Earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

In July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The company seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

SpaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing customers to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Significant Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the company intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

#3208. Industry News: The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (646 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (646 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.
  • Industry observers note that your Windows installation depends on a collection of important system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks.
  • Industry observers note that DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.

Industry observers note that your Windows installation depends on a collection of important system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks. If these files get damaged or go missing, your system may behave erratically. You may encounter system errors, features not working as expected, freezes or other unexpected behavior. Sometimes restarting your computer or running the usual troubleshooting steps aren't enough to restore damaged system files. For such cases, Windows provides a built-in repair utility called Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM).

Industry observers note that DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs. Particularly, there are three useful DISM commands that achieve this purpose: CheckHealth, ScanHealth and RestoreHealth. You can run DISM commands in either the command prompt or the PowerShell, but both CLIs require administrator privileges to make system-level changes. It's worth noting that DISM exclusively scans and repairs system files; your personal files remain untouched.

All three DISM commands in question follow a specific syntax that begins with DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image. The parts following "DISM" in the syntax are called command-line options. The /Online CLI option specifies DISM to take action on the currently running Windows installation, while /Cleanup-Image performs recovery operations on the selected installation.

Industry observers note that the first command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth. It checks whether Windows has already flagged corrupt system files and whether the corruption is repairable. This is the first recommended step when investigating corrupt system files as it takes very little time to complete.

Sources indicate that the next command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth and it works slightly differently from the CheckHealth command. Unlike CheckHealth, the ScanHealth DISM command performs a fresh scan of your system files and reports any its findings. The ScanHealth operation may take several minutes to complete, but it provides you with a fresh report on the component store's health.

Finally, the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth command both scans the component store for corruption and attempts to repair them automatically. By default, RestoreHealth uses Windows Upgrade to obtain the necessary system files needed to repair the component store. The Windows component store is a protected internal repository that contains crucial system files. Windows requires these files to service, update and customize the operating system.

Industry observers note that sometimes system file damage can also break Windows Enhancement, preventing DISM from downloading replacement files. When this happens, you can use an official Windows installation media to supply DISM with the necessary repair files. You can download a Windows ISO from Microsoft's official download page. Once downloaded, right click the ISO file and select mount. Windows will create a virtual drive for the ISO, assign it a drive letter and make its contents available.

Next, you'll need to check the Windows editions available in the downloaded installation media. You can do that by launching the command prompt as an administrator and running the DISM /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:D:sourcesinstall.wim command. This command lists the Windows editions available on the installation media along with their index numbers. Make a note of the index number corresponding to your installed edition before proceeding to the next step.

Now, run the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:WIM:D:sourcesinstall.wim:6 /LimitAccess command. Replace D: with the drive letter assigned to the mounted Windows ISO and 6 with the index number corresponding to your Windows edition. This directs DISM to use the installation media as its repair source instead of downloading files from Windows Upgrade.

In a recent development, once DISM completes its operation, run the sfc /scannow command to repair damaged or missing system files. Microsoft recommends running the DISM repair utility before System File Checker (SFC) because DISM repairs the Windows component store, which SFC relies on to replace corrupted system files.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US Commerce Department has put Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud organization at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, on its trade blacklist, after officials and lawmakers spent weeks asking why it was taking so long.

Moreover, the Entity List filing also caught six firms seen as Megaspeed affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

I’ve led the push for the Department of Commerce to crack down on Megaspeed. I’m glad it’s finally moving forward.

In a recent development, the Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Congress why this took so long. Other agencies including the Departments of State, Treasury, and War supported the designation.

— Senator Pete Ricketts (@SenatorRicketts) November 23, 2026.

A place on the list means US firms need a licence to sell it goods, software, or tech, and such requests are usually refused. Listed firms also struggle to get spare parts and updates for gear they already run.

Industry observers note that US investigators have spent more than a year looking into whether Megaspeed, long one of Nvidia’s bigger customers, funnelled advanced chips into China, where export rules bar their sale. The Justice Department has opened a criminal inquiry, and Nvidia says it chose to stop selling to the firm in June 2025.

In a recent development, why the listing took so long had become a sore point at the top of the US government. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about it at a White House meeting this month, Axios reported, though Commerce indicates that never happened.

Four departments had wanted Megaspeed listed for months, but “commerce has the pen,” Bessent told CNBC this month.

According to recent reports, the scandal runs through the company’s former boss, Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang. US spy agencies reportedly came to suspect her of working for Chinese intelligence, a claim that was not confirmed until now.

Nvidia investigates after CEO admits affair linked to spy reports.

Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 11 November, after 33 years running the tech giant he co-founded. On the same day Megaspeed was blacklisted, Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate him.

Megaspeed denies doing anything wrong and says Alice Huang left the company in August 2025. The rule took effect on Monday, when it was filed for public inspection, and formal publication in the Federal Register follows on Wednesday.

Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
  • In a recent development, after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
  • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a newly introduced Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber indicates that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

In a recent development, after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Industry observers note that starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

Uber claims the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

Industry observers note that uber notes it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

In a recent development, uber claims it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, filled with photos and memes reflecting the game's satirical rendition of the U.S.
  • As such, GTA 6 players have discovered that Snapmatic can be used to identify robbery targets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) has been out for less than a week, but players have already found a plethora of considered details in the massive sandbox game. Among them is a novel method players are using to get more money in GTA 6, helping them find robbery targets that are worth their time. It also doubles as an important reminder about internet safety.

Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, filled with photos and memes reflecting the game's satirical rendition of the U.S. This includes people showing off drugs, cars, and weapons in a bid for clout. Like Instagram, Snapmatic also allows its fictional consumers to tag a location in their posts.

As such, GTA 6 players have discovered that Snapmatic can be used to identify robbery targets. Simply find a post with a location tagged, and open the menu you'd use to like it or view comments. Under the "Like" option will be "Set Destination," which will mark the location of the Snapmatic post on your map. You can then head there to relieve characters of their belongings (typically via the use of notable violence).

Sources indicate that it's an interesting gameplay mechanic that also serves as a reminder to be careful about what you post online. While the world of GTA 6 is a heightened version of reality, it does still have some basis in truth. There have been multiple real-life instances of criminals finding their victims via social media posts, something that's been occurring for years.

It has been revealed that last month, a UK man was convicted of stealing £48,000 (about $62,900) and various items from a home after seeing the family's social media posts indicating they'd be out hosting a Chinese Latest Year celebration. In 2021, four people were arrested in Italy for allegedly stealing from celebrities and influencers after monitoring their Instagram accounts, reportedly using victims' posts to identify tagged locations, entry points, and when they'd be away from home. Back in 2016, a California man was convicted of stealing personal items from female college students after finding them via GPS locations in photos posted to Instagram.

Even if you exclude location tags and don't mention your movements in your posts, you can still be vulnerable. Late last year, four French men travelled to Australia in order to rob a home of items reportedly valued at around $AU10 million ($6.6 million). According to court documents, the thieves saw photos of luxury goods that a victim had posted to Instagram, as well as images of their backyard and local surroundings. The thieves then used ChatGPT to search for where these pictures were taken, narrowing it down to a specific Australian city and suburb, which helped them locate the house.

Industry observers note that using social media to pick robbery targets in GTA 6 won't attract the same legal consequences and prison time that it would in real life. Rather, it serves as a neat little trick to help ambitious, self-starting criminals find worthwhile heists. However, this mechanic should also serve as an key reminder about the dangers of real-life Insta-bragging, and a warning to be careful about what you share online. It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) offers a satirical rendition of the U.S., filled with cars, crime, and shenanigans worthy of the game's Florida-inspired setting. It also incorporates many digital elements of modern life, including social media. Of course, where there's social media, there are inevitably memes.

In-game social media app Snapmatic is GTA 6's version of Instagram, offering a scrollable feed of posts from fictional characters showing off their very lootable possessions. However, Snapmatic isn't just filled with posts sharing potential theft coordinates. It also contains a plethora of memes specifically created to populate GTA 6's social media.

Players quickly took note of GTA 6's memes, praising them for accurately capturing the irreverent vibe and frequently off-colour humour that typically characterises such media.

"GTA 6 is so realistic that I thought this was a real meme," posted X user @thisdopenose, sharing an image of an in-game meme. In the meme, the text "bisexuals when they realise you can have sex more than twice" is edited onto a monochrome image of a man crying. The popular post has 94,000 likes at time of writing.

"They need to give a pay rise to whoever came up with the shitposts on Snapmatic bro these things are so funny," wrote @vandalfeet.

Some of GTA 6's in-game memes even referred to memes about GTA 6 itself. It's been 13 years since GTA 5 released, with many fans having eagerly awaited the franchises' latest instalment for over a decade. In the interim, it became a common meme for people to jokingly express disbelief that various other events had occurred "before GTA 6" arrived.

Developer Rockstar Games appears to have been aware of such memes, creating its own versions referring to GTA 6's fictional video game Race and Chase 7. ("Race'n'Chase" was the original working title for the first Grand Theft Auto game released in 1997).

Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games had teams dedicated to creating in-game media, aiming to flesh out GTA 6's world and make it feel more immersive. Judging by fans' reactions, it appears to have paid off. Parent firm Take-Two Interactive estimates that GTA 6 achieved $3.79 billion in sales on day one alone, making it one of the biggest entertainment media rolls out ever. Nintendo Store — Out of stock right now, but you can add it to your wishlist to get pinged the second a restock hits.

Landing limited-edition Nintendo hardware takes a little prep work, but these battle-tested habits will give you a real edge over the bots:.

Hands off the refresh button in Best Buy's queue — When an online drop goes live, Best Buy puts shoppers into a randomized waiting line to filter out scrapers. Touching the reload button resets your spot and boots you straight to the back.

Dodge third-party sellers — Double-check the seller before buying. Marketplace scalpers frequently list units for jacked-up prices; make sure it claims "Sold and shipped by [Retailer]" at the standard price.

Skip the web wars and head to physical stores — Online checkout bots grab website stock in under 15 seconds. Showing up in person is easily your most reliable path to securing one without paying scalper markups.
